detail: Two ci.yml jobs were red for the same reason and both were green locally, which is why neither was caught before pushing. signature-parity loaded the host-pure signature exports out of runners/rn/runner.mjs, but that bundle imported webdriverio at top level, so the pure functions could not load without the Appium driver in a job that installs no npm packages; it passed locally only because runners/rn/node_modules happened to exist. sdk-backend-core pinned an exact `deployment` shape while Capture.resolve_commit deliberately falls back to GITHUB_SHA, which a GitHub runner always sets and a laptop never does, so the batch grew a `commit` key only in CI. The fix defers the webdriverio import to the one call site that starts a session, and gives the Python suite a conftest that clears the ambient code-identity variables. Both defects live in gate wiring and packaging, so no runtime guard can hold them; the bounded regression test is structural in the same spirit as check-harness-integrity.py, asserting that the bundle has no static webdriverio import but still has the dynamic one (so deleting the dependency cannot pass), and that the conftest actually clears the variables it names. A third instance of the same class was then found, and it is the worst because it produced no red at all: the native-backend-gates job `windows-uia` is pinned to a self-hosted runner, of which this repository has zero registered, but its condition `event_name != 'workflow_dispatch' || inputs.run_windows_uia` ran it on every push and skipped it on the only event that can opt in, inverting its own declared default of false. A run stays queued until every job concludes, so the workflow never reported red or green on 12 consecutive pushes over several hours. The fix matches macos-ax, which was already correctly opt-in, and the fourth structural case asserts that any job needing a self-hosted runner is workflow_dispatch-gated and rejects the inverted `!=` form specifically. All four cases fail on the parent and pass on the fix.
